players.product: AI/automotive chip designer - Samsung Foundry contract-manufacturing customer (USD 16.5B, 2025-2033)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results (Vaibhav Taneja): vehicle deliveries above 480K for a second consecutive quarter; automotive gross margin excluding credits rose sequentially from 16.3% to 18.1% on a higher APAC delivery mix, with commodity prices and interest rates still headwinds; energy storage deployments of 13.7 GWh, the second-best quarter, and energy gross margin up from 20.4% to 33.1%, mainly on tariff refunds recognized and warranty true-downs after a vendor agreed to reimburse certain cell-related costs; services and other margin an all-time high of 15.9% (from 14.1%), with Supercharging and insurance strong. Operating expenses rose again on AI development (compute depreciation, chip development) and pre-production costs for Optimus, Megapack 3 and the Semi, a trend expected to continue until these products are commercialized. Free cash flow over $1.5 billion; cash and investments over $45 billion. The Model Y was, on preliminary data, the number one selling BEV in Europe and the number one selling passenger car in South Korea.
quarterly_data.figure: deliveries >480K; automotive margin ex credits 18.1%; energy storage 13.7 GWh, energy margin 33.1%; free cash flow >$1.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook: Vaibhav Taneja: 2026 capex guidance revised to approximately $20 billion, funded primarily from operating cash flow, and capex will keep expanding over the next few years for the Robotaxi fleet, Optimus capacity, solar manufacturing, additional AI compute and a semiconductor fab; Elon Musk: capex is 'ending up being a little lower than we anticipated' but will become more meaningful next year and 'noticeable in the tens of billions in 2028'. Musk: Tesla is aiming for 5 million vehicles a year by approximately 2030 and expects Megapack gross margins 'to increase meaningfully'. On Robotaxi economics Taneja expects it to become 'a significant part of our revenue and profitability in 2027'; Taneja answered 'Exactly' to a remark, whose speaker the transcript does not label, that it 'starts to become noticeable probably in Q2 and then probably a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex approximately $20 billion; 5 million vehicles a year by approximately 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and backlog (Elon Musk, Vaibhav Taneja): vehicle demand is exceeding production 'by a significant margin', with FSD the biggest driver; Tesla exited the quarter with its highest automotive backlog in four years. Energy: Tesla is 'almost sold out of all Megapacks for 2027', sees 'extreme demand from data centers' and is ramping production as fast as possible, expecting ASP and margin improvements; deliveries of Megapacks with Tesla's in-house LFP batteries began in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: highest automotive backlog in four years; Megapacks almost sold out for 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Production capacity (Vaibhav Taneja, Lars Moravy): deliveries are constrained primarily by production; factories ran at record rates this quarter as earlier strategic investments to raise rates come to fruition, but can only build 'at the rate of the least lucky process or component'. Tesla applied for permits to expand the Berlin factory, just started its new Semi factory in Reno (Semi production began in Q3), and is ramping Cybercab at Giga Texas; Moravy: Cybercab has 50% fewer parts than any previous Tesla vehicle and the line's actual capacity is 'significantly higher' than its listed rate, currently run at the pace the Robotaxi service needs. Tariff refunds are being reinvested in U.S. production capacity.

Upcoming milestones: Ashok Elluswamy: Cybercab launches in Dallas next month, and customer cars could join the Robotaxi fleet around Q2 next year with the V15 software release; Lars Moravy: Tesla is trying to get Cybercabs to customers by the end of 2026; Vaibhav Taneja: Cybercab will reach other cities before year end. Elon Musk: EU-wide FSD approval maybe within a few months ('I would be surprised if it takes longer than Q1'); an Optimus video in a month or two; the AI5 chip integrated into Optimus 'if things go according to plan' in approximately April next year, with 'an order of magnitude more compute' than AI4; Optimus deliveries to companies outside Tesla around the end of next year, first for industrial uses. Terafab: the Austin research fab begins commissioning machinery in the first half of next year, a first test chip is hoped for around May or June, useful chips at volume are the aspiration for around Q3 2028 and 'real production would be late 2028'.
quarterly_data.figure: Dallas Cybercab launch next month; AI5 in Optimus around April next year; Terafab first test chip around May or June next year

quarterly_data.signal: Robotaxi and FSD (Elon Musk, Vaibhav Taneja, Ashok Elluswamy): the Cybercab fleet in Austin has grown by a factor of 10 since launch about a month ago and cumulative unsupervised miles rose 8x in the quarter with double-digit weekly growth; Robotaxi runs in six cities, service hours are extending toward 2:00 A.M., and 24/7 operation and higher-speed roads are to be unlocked this year. Over 75% of North American deliveries in Q3 included a paid FSD subscription sign-up at delivery, about 20% higher than Q2 (every car comes with a month of free FSD); FSD has over 1.7 million paid customers globally, 50% on subscriptions for the first time. Taneja agreed with an analyst's estimate that FSD recurring revenue is approaching $1 billion a year ('I think the numbers which you shared are correct') and said more FSD metrics will be disclosed. Robotaxi is not yet at the $0.30 per mile target, but Taneja sees a path to it; Tesla is building its own AI-based mapping and navigation, starting with V15.
quarterly_data.figure: FSD over 1.7 million paid customers; >75% North America attach at delivery; unsupervised miles 8x in Q3

quarterly_data.signal: Optimus and Terafab (Elon Musk, Vaibhav Taneja): early production has started on the high-volume Optimus line in Fremont, where 'the vast majority of a million unit per line production line' has landed; reaching that annualized rate will take 'at least a year, maybe a little longer' because parts of the design are still changing; in the Q&A a management speaker the transcript does not label named the hand as the main remaining electromechanical challenge. Tesla needs on the order of 10,000 or 20,000 robots doing self-play in an 'Optimus Academy' for training data; construction has started on an Austin factory able to build more robots than Fremont; Optimus cost is trending toward where Cybercab costs would end up. Terafab will need capital 'certainly in the tens of billions' through early 2028 and 'probably north of $100 billion long term', with the split between SpaceX and Tesla still to be worked out; Taneja: Tesla has already placed most of the orders for the first set of research-fab equipment. Musk on Megapod (distributed compute): 'still early days', with a better sense by end of Q1 or Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: million-unit Optimus line in Fremont; Terafab tens of billions through early 2028, north of $100 billion long term
